chapter: Small groups, Europe and Kansas City memories (repeated passages)
title: End of the big-band years, small groups and the Mahogany Hall band in Boston
summary: After Basie and Carter he worked with smaller groups, and directed a band at Mahogany Hall in Boston with players such as Doc Cheatham and a bassist who painted a face on his instrument.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: When we were sort of talking about your associations before -- I guess we -- your careet -- we
got to Basie and then back to Benny , and then I guess that was just about the end of your big band career --
Yeah, it was. Yes it was because then I started getting a strike. Smaller groups -- Frankie Newton and Sidney Bechet, Eddie Hayward, and Hollywood, and Bobby Hackett --
Uh-huh.
I did some (inaudible) and you know -- (one minute inaudible).
(Inaudible).
It wasn't my band -- I just directed it.
Were you at the Savoy in London?
No, I played the Savoy with Thamon Hall. Then I had this -- this band I was directing was down at the -- called Mahogany Hall in Boston.
Oh yeah, yeah. That was George Williamson.
Yeah. I was kind of like in charge of the band but it wasn't none of my bands you know.
Is that the band with Claude Hotter (PHONETIC) (inaudible)
Yeah.
-- Doc and .
Buzzy Newton --
Buzzy and his brother Al --
Yeah.
And John Field (PHONETIC).
Yeah, John --
He was a character. He had a face painted on his bass.
Yeah.

Yeah, (unintelligible). John on the bass you know.
Oh, there's so many when you get to --
Yeah.
